meta.note: These rates are frozen. This tool makes no network calls, which means it cannot be wrong about a rate it never fetched, but it also means the numbers age. Each rate below carries the date it was read and where it came from. Where an official rate and a street rate differ, both are shown, because in several of these countries the official rate is not the rate you can actually transact at.

rates.name: US dollar
rates.note: The unit everything here is measured in.

rates.name: Euro
rates.note: Derived from the ECB reference rate of 1 EUR = 1.1234 USD.

rates.name: British pound
rates.note: Derived from ECB cross rates (GBP 0.83825 per EUR, USD 1.1234 per EUR).

rates.name: Lebanese pound
rates.source: Banque du Liban, current exchange rates page
rates.note: The date on this figure is the date printed on the Banque du Liban page, not today. The official rate moved from 1,507.5 to 15,000 in February 2023 and to 89,500 in early 2024.

rates.name: UAE dirham
rates.source: Central Bank of the UAE, domestic market operations
rates.note: Pegged. The central bank intervenes automatically at 3.672 buying and 3.673 selling. Holding dirhams is close to holding dollars, for as long as the peg holds.

rates.name: Egyptian pound
rates.source: Central Bank of Egypt official rate
rates.note: Midpoint of the CBE buying rate of 54.3377 and selling rate of 54.4377. Any parallel-market gap is unverified here.

rates.name: Turkish lira
rates.source: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkey, bulletin 2026/199
rates.note: Midpoint of the CBRT buying rate of 49.5123 and selling rate of 49.6015.

rates.name: Nigerian naira
rates.source: Central Bank of Nigeria central rate
rates.note: CBN central rate (buy 1,333.72, sell 1,334.72). Street rates were about 1,365 to 1,380, roughly 3 percent weaker, per Vanguard on 21 October 2026.

rates.name: Argentine peso
rates.source: Banco Central de la República Argentina, Comunicación A 3500 wholesale reference
rates.note: Comunicación A 3500 (BCRA series 5). The blue rate was about 1,545 to 1,565 and the contado con liquidación rate about 1,633 on 21 October 2026. Argentines have lived with several simultaneous exchange rates for years.
